_source: WinoBias (Zhao et al. 2018, NAACL), https://github.com/uclanlp/corefBias - MIT licence
_selection: The sixty pairs the kids level runs on, vetted by hand for classroom use: violence, insults, crime and coarse wording are filtered out, and the remainder is sampled at a fixed stride so many occupations are covered. Within a pair the two sentences differ in the pronoun and in nothing else. Above the kids level the instrument draws afresh from the whole checked pool instead - see devserver/my_app/services/winobias_corpus.py.
_de: Helper translation for readers who are not fluent in English. The occupation stays in English and carries the German pair in parentheses ("the physician (Arzt/Ärztin)"). German marks gender on the occupation noun, so a plain translation would resolve exactly what the sentence has to leave open.
_corrections: Three annotation spans were truncated in the source and offered a non-person as the second option. Corrected here: type1-val-37 "The construction" -> "The construction worker", type1-val-127 "the application" -> "the editor", type1-tes-255 "the documents" -> "the clerk".
_removals: Two removals. WinoBias carries a stray "he" in type1 test item 216, so that pair's two sentences no longer differ in the pronoun alone; it was dropped rather than edited and replaced by test item 215, which stands one step earlier in the same raster and covers the same two occupations. And on 2026-08-21 the whole type1 group left this file: WinoBias resolves it by "world knowledge" the paper never checked, and Blodgett et al. (ACL 2021) count only 22 percent of its pairs as unaffected by the defects they inventory, against 38 percent for type2. On 2026-08-22 test item 151 was dropped as well: "The tailor stopped the guard and showed him identification." against "... showed her identification." - English "her" is both the object form and the possessive determiner, so the second sentence reads just as well as "showed [her identification]", where the pronoun is not a reference to a person at all. The two sentences then differ in more than the pronoun and the pair asks something other than what the instrument measures. Replaced by tes item 150, which stands nearby in the same raster and does not carry the same construction.

_groups.type2: The sentence structure fixes the referent; the answer can be read off the sentence.
